method: Static bytecode decompilation, offline resource decoding and native control-flow analysis; no sample program or fetched C2 payload executed. Atomscan and cleave facts were run on all originals.

execution_trace: The only member is package/package.json. preinstall Base64-encodes the constant data and prints it; test echoes ok.
postinstall launches Python, reads /etc/hosts in binary mode, Base64-encodes the bytes into body, then passes body as httpx.post content to an OASTify URL.
There is one distinct hostile result: install-triggered network-configuration exfiltration. No downloaded or dropped payload is present; three hostile behaviors would be invented.

A deliberately simple OAST probe could be an authorized security test, but the package provides no disclosure or authorization context. Its automatic export of a machine file tips the machine-triage verdict to malicious.

samples.identification: Donki-style Java credential and file stealer
execution_trace: Manifest entrypoint com.example.Main calls initialize. It uses RPCHelper.getVerifiedText to resolve its HTTPS server from an Ethereum eth_call result, then builds /api/receive endpoints.

Main.initialize obtains DiscordHandler.getDiscordTokens, BrowserHandler.getBrowserInfo, FileHandler.getDonkiFiles and system information. It serializes userData to a JSON POST and uploads collected file bytes as multipart bodies.

PasswordHandler copies Chromium Login Data and Login Data For Account, opens SQLite, queries origin_url/username_value/password_value, decrypts password_value through gcmDecrypt, and builds JSON records. Locked files can be duplicated from process handles or copied after terminating the browser.

FirefoxHandler uses key4.db/logins.json, NSS_Init and PK11SDR_Decrypt to recover logins, and copies/queries cookies.sqlite. DiscordHandler searches LevelDB for plain/encrypted tokens, decrypts them and validates them against /users/@me with Authorization.

FileHandler targets desktop and browser-extension wallets, Minecraft and other application credentials. WHandler downloads replacements and overwrites Exodus resources/app.asar and Discord desktop-core index.js.

StagingHelper.stage constructs hidden PowerShell that DownloadString-fetches /api/static/update and invokes ScriptBlock.Create. cmstpBypass writes an INF with RunPreSetupCommands, launches cmstp.exe /au and automatically confirms its dialog through User32.SendMessage, then deletes the INF.

Offline reconstruction of Dec.s: strings.bin has a u24 count and u24 lengths. Per-string state is SEED xor (index * -7046029254386353131); each byte advances the 64-bit LCG by 6364136223846793005 and 1442695040888963407 and XORs bits 32..39. No sample code was executed.

Silent third-party secret export, application-code replacement and elevation bypass distinguish this program from an authorized password migration tool. Bundled Gson metadata does not identify the enclosing program.
This is an unsigned x64 DLL despite the .exe suffix. Its export is KKHS in poolparty6.dll; initial loading/invocation context is unavailable.

KKHS at VA 0x180007f00 probes security-product processes, calls installation logic at 0x180004a60 and Restart Manager logic at 0x180007d80, then transfers to the Explorer injection routine at 0x1800071b0.

Installation copies local staging files, copies PowerShell under a different executable name, constructs shortcuts with Base64-file-to-Unicode-IEX arguments, and writes AutoHotkey code that redirects Explorer User Shell Folders Startup, opens a shortcut through Explorer, and hides/closes launcher windows. The referenced external b64 script body is not contained in this DLL.

Injection constructs explorer.exe on the stack, enumerates its PID, opens the process, allocates executable remote memory, writes the 3032-byte buffer at VA 0x1800b72f0, and supplies that same allocation to CreateRemoteThread.

The embedded thread stage was carved from .data at file offset 0xb52f0. It walks PEB modules and PE exports, hashes names with BKDR131 and masks the sign bit, and resolves LoadLibraryA, VirtualAlloc/Free, RtlZero/MoveMemory and Winsock functions.

Resolved Winsock hashes: WSAStartup=33522634, socket=26402d9f, getaddrinfo=41539501, freeaddrinfo=785e7dd7, htons=313a84c8, connect=092b50da, send=0f8387dc, recv=0f6134b2, closesocket=14ac161b, WSACleanup=4ff42ccf.

The stage connects to a configured endpoint, sends a 64 architecture marker, receives code into allocated storage, applies a counter-wrapped XOR loop, calls the reconstructed buffer, and invokes its returned entrypoint with configuration. No final server-supplied stage was retrieved or executed.

Restart Manager registers file paths derived from 360tray.exe processes and requests shutdown. Unwanted Startup redirection, interpreter disguise, security interference and Explorer injection tip the verdict to malicious; no named family is inferred.

corrections: Base64-word lifecycle predicates retain their matchers and scopes, move to direction-neutral codec-reference homes, and become notable. Literal mentions and honest encoding do not establish obfuscation.
OASTify URL/host predicates move unchanged to the neutral callback-host home and become notable. An endpoint reference establishes neither contact nor theft.

The /etc/hosts postinstall predicate is a path reference, not a read: its unchanged matcher moves to fs/path/config/system and becomes notable. A separate operation-constrained read-beside-POST observation supports the new exfiltration detection.
Inline Python plus a URL is a script declaration, not evidence of fetching: its unchanged matcher moves to metadata/package/scripts/command and becomes notable.

The two old npm hostile findings represented the same source/encoding/endpoint co-occurrence, lacked a required transfer and could pool unrelated hook content. They are replaced by one operation-constrained, same-postinstall exfiltration finding. All supported attack behavior is retained on the real package and the existing positive archive fixture.
The unused obfuscated-script OR of evaluator and codec references was removed because neither alternative establishes obfuscation. Its evaluator and codec constituent observations remain.

A Unicode.GetString-to-IEX pattern did not require Base64 or maliciousness: it moves unchanged to neutral interpreter evaluation and becomes notable. The hostile PowerShell composite now requires a Base64 decoder, policy bypass, and Startup-loader context.

Unsigned Explorer injection APIs alone did not establish malicious intent. The hostile finding now requires the independently supported Startup-script loader context and is renamed explorer-startup-script-injector. The neutral injection API profile remains on the positive sample and all four native controls.

Registry command/value atoms leave the persistence objective. The Startup value argument is retained under registry/value-name; the reg-add verb uses the canonical generic write token beside the existing key-path observation. The hostile persistence composite additionally requires the staged interpreter and copy context.

Two install-command regexes were equivalent under identical shell/PowerShell scopes: (npm|pnpm|yarn|bun)/(add|install|i) versus (p?npm|yarn|bun)/(add|i(nstall)?). The duplicate was consolidated without losing any matched command. Twelve command controls and existing fixture references retain coverage.
consumer_audit: All exact active YAML references to moved IDs were updated. Historical comparison snapshots were not rewritten.
The three ancestor selectors for data/encode/base64 have JavaScript/TypeScript/shell/Python scope; relocated predicates are package.json-only, so their effective matched populations are unchanged.

Two ancestor OAST consumers previously treated bare endpoints as theft. They retain actual behavioral descendants, while neutral endpoint-only corroboration no longer supplies a theft finding. This is an intentional unsupported-claim correction.

A trial broadening of the generic npm POST predicate exposed an unrelated preinstall attribution on the postinstall sender. It was reverted. The new detection instead requires reading and POST code in the same postinstall value.
coverage_limits: Npm has one supported hostile result, so the 3-5 goal is intentionally unmet. Preinstall only encodes/prints a constant; there is no evidence for payload acquisition, execution, persistence or additional theft.

The Java archive already has credential acquisition, exfiltration and concealment detections, and now also CMSTP elevation-bypass coverage. Specific wallet targets and Exodus/Discord replacement paths were recovered offline but live in a cross-class encrypted resource. Current file-local string matchers cannot correlate those decoded resource entries to each calling class; no plaintext-only rule or helper-name conviction was invented.

The native injected network-stage loader is now detected independently of its IP or campaign configuration. The external PowerShell body and server-supplied final native stage are unavailable in the sample, so their behavior is not asserted.

After accurate npm corrections, classifier hostile_fp_level changes from 0 to -1 even though the concrete exfiltration trait fires. This is a classifier miss, not grounds to restore inaccurate traits. Java and native remain above the hostile gate (level 25). The scanner warns that its v18 feature specification predates v21 analyzer features.

focused_verification.native_controls: renamed positive; removed Winsock hash; removed XOR handoff; removed script activation. Neutral injection coverage retained in all.
focused_verification.rule_changes: No inline YARA edits; precompilation is unnecessary.
